title: Why can a Java 8 → 11 upgrade break the build (removed Java EE / CORBA modules now needing explicit dependencies)?
shortTitle: Java 8→11 upgrade — removed Java EE/CORBA modules breaking builds
topicTitle: Why can a Java 8 → 11 upgrade break the build

s1_definition.profdef: Java 11 removed six Java EE and CORBA modules that were in the JDK since Java 1.x: `java.xml.ws` (JAX-WS/SOAP), `java.xml.bind` (JAXB), `java.activation` (JAF), `java.xml.ws.annotation` (Common Annotations), `java.corba` (CORBA), `java.transaction` (JTA). These were deprecated in Java 9 (via `@Deprecated(forRemoval=true)`) and removed in Java 11. Code using `javax.xml.bind.JAXB`, `javax.annotation.PostConstruct`, `javax.xml.ws.Service` fails with `ClassNotFoundException` or `NoClassDefFoundError` after upgrading. Fix: add explicit Maven/Gradle dependencies for these libraries (now maintained by Jakarta EE).
s1_definition.analogy: Java 8 was a building with a cafeteria, gym, and childcare (Java EE modules) included free. Java 11 removed them: "These services are available across the street (Maven Central) — we're not bundling them anymore." If your code relied on the in-building cafeteria (JAXB for XML), it breaks until you explicitly order food delivery (add the Maven dependency).
s1_definition.oneliner: Java 11 removed: JAXB, JAX-WS, JAF, Common Annotations, CORBA, JTA. Fix: add jakarta.xml.bind-api, jakarta.annotation-api as Maven dependencies. javax.* → jakarta.* namespace.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Java 11 removed six Java EE and CORBA modules that were in the JDK since Java 1.x: `java.xml.ws` (JAX-WS/SOAP), `java.xml.bind` (JAXB), `java.activation` (JAF), `java.xml.ws.annotation` (Common Annotations), `java.corba` (CORBA), `java.transaction` (JTA). These were deprecated in Java 9 (via `@Deprecated(forRemoval=true)`) and removed in Java 11. Code using `javax.xml.bind.JAXB`, `javax.annotation.PostConstruct`, `javax.xml.ws.Service` fails with `ClassNotFoundException` or `NoClassDefFoundError` after upgrading. Fix: add explicit Maven/Gradle dependencies for these libraries (now maintained by Jakarta EE).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Java 8 was a building with a cafeteria, gym, and childcare (Java EE modules) included free. Java 11 removed them: "These services are available across the street (Maven Central) — we're not bundling them anymore." If your code relied on the in-building cafeteria (JAXB for XML), it breaks until you explicitly order food delivery (add the Maven dependency).

**One line to remember:** Java 11 removed: JAXB, JAX-WS, JAF, Common Annotations, CORBA, JTA. Fix: add jakarta.xml.bind-api, jakarta.annotation-api as Maven dependencies. javax.* → jakarta.* namespace.

sections.s2_technical:
Upgrading from Java 8 to Java 11 is mostly smooth at the language level, but the big breaking change is the removal of modules that were deprecated for removal in Java 9 and deleted in Java 11. The Java EE and CORBA modules — JAXB (`java.xml.bind`), JAX-WS (`java.xml.ws`), JAF (`java.activation`), Common Annotations (`java.xml.ws.annotation`), and CORBA (`java.corba`) — are gone from the JDK.

Code that used these now fails to compile or run with `ClassNotFoundException`/`NoClassDefFoundError` for classes like `javax.xml.bind.JAXBContext`. The fix is to add them back as explicit Maven/Gradle dependencies (for example `jakarta.xml.bind:jakarta.xml.bind-api` plus a runtime implementation). Other changes: some internal `sun.*` APIs are inaccessible under the module system, and the default GC became G1.

A banking example: a legacy service that marshals XML messages with JAXB breaks on Java 11 until the JAXB API and runtime are added as dependencies. Senior nuance: run `jdeps --jdk-internals your.jar` before upgrading to find uses of removed modules and internal APIs, so you fix them proactively rather than at runtime.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — A legacy XML-messaging service compiled on Java 8 failed on Java 11 with `ClassNotFoundException: javax.xml.bind.JAXBContext` because the Java EE modules were removed. Fix: add JAXB back as an explicit dependency (jakarta.xml.bind API plus a runtime), and run `jdeps` to find any other removed-module or internal-API usage before the upgrade.

```xml
<!-- JAXB (XML binding) — was in JDK, now separate -->

    <groupId>jakarta.xml.bind</groupId>
    <artifactId>jakarta.xml.bind-api</artifactId>
    <version>4.0.0</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.glassfish.jaxb</groupId>
    <artifactId>jaxb-runtime</artifactId>
    <version>4.0.3</version>
</dependency>

<!-- Common Annotations (@PostConstruct, @PreDestroy) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>jakarta.annotation</groupId>
    <artifactId>jakarta.annotation-api</artifactId>
    <version>2.1.1</version>
</dependency>

<!-- JAX-WS (SOAP web services) -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>jakarta.xml.ws</groupId>
    <artifactId>jakarta.xml.ws-api</artifactId>

</dependency>

<!-- Activation Framework -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>jakarta.activation</groupId>
    <artifactId>jakarta.activation-api</artifactId>
    <version>2.1.2</version>
</dependency>
```

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: the service's class references scanned before upgrading to Java 11.

**Step 2.** `jdeps --jdk-internals` lists references to removed Java EE/CORBA modules like `javax.xml.bind.JAXBContext`.

**Step 3.** Each reference is classified: removed-module classes must be re-added as dependencies; core classes like `java.util.stream.Stream` are fine.

**Step 4.** The JAXB API and a runtime implementation are added to the build so marshalling works again.

**Step 5.** After adding the dependencies, the service compiles and runs on Java 11.

```text
INFO: javax.xml.bind=REMOVED, add dependency; java.util.stream=OK
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ MODULES REMOVED IN JAVA 11 ═══

  Module                      │ Used for                    │ Replacement dependency
  ────────────────────────────│─────────────────────────────│──────────────────────────
  java.xml.bind (JAXB)       │ XML ↔ Java binding          │ jakarta.xml.bind-api
  java.xml.ws (JAX-WS)       │ SOAP web services           │ jakarta.xml.ws-api
  java.activation (JAF)      │ MIME data handling           │ jakarta.activation-api
  java.xml.ws.annotation     │ @PostConstruct, @Resource   │ jakarta.annotation-api
  java.corba                  │ CORBA (obsolete)            │ (removed, rarely needed)
  java.transaction (JTA)     │ Distributed transactions    │ jakarta.transaction-api

  ═══ COMMON ERRORS AFTER UPGRADE ═══

  ClassNotFoundException: javax.xml.bind.JAXBContext
  NoClassDefFoundError: javax/annotation/PostConstruct
  → Fix: add the Jakarta dependency to pom.xml
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
A Java 8 to 11 upgrade commonly breaks builds because Java 11 removed six Java EE modules that were bundled in the JDK: JAXB, JAX-WS, JAF, Common Annotations, CORBA, and JTA. Code using `@PostConstruct`, JAXB marshalling, or SOAP clients gets `ClassNotFoundException`. The fix is adding explicit Maven dependencies — the modules are now maintained under the `jakarta.*` namespace (Jakarta EE). Spring Boot 3.x already includes these as transitive dependencies, but standalone Java applications must add them manually. This is the single most common Java 8→11 migration issue.
